newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial shares end weak in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial shares end weak in thin trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares traded largely weaker on Tuesday, with brokers saying investors had come onto the market looking for bargains and but many were convinced some counters were over-valued.
"There was a bit of profit-taking, but volumes were thin on the buying side with lower bids from people who strongly feel some shares are over-valued," one broker commented.

The 57-counter industrial index dropped 18.49 points to 6,764.89 following losses in several stocks, including banking group Finhold, winer producer Afdis and clothing retailers Truworths, which traded 10 cents lower at 930, 50 cents down at 340 and also 50 cents softer at 550 respectively.

Zimbabwe share analysts say they expect the market to trade generally firmer into the new year on investor hopes good rains in the farming season starting in November will help boost the country's agriculture-based economy.
On Tuesday, the secondary seven-share mining index plunged 127.02 points to 1,241.96, following a 1,700-cent plunge in gold giants Ashanti which traded at 14,000.
